clue.text: One hard man, he was involved with Ezra initially

definitions.text: One hard man, he was involved with Ezra initially

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of Ezra

parts.note: first letter of Ezra

explanation.surface: A tough character who worked alongside Ezra in the early days.
explanation.walkthrough: Nehemiah and Ezra worked together rebuilding Jerusalem, and the book of Nehemiah follows the book of Ezra in the Bible, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Nehemiah was the Jewish governor who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls, a contemporary and collaborator of the scribe in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Considered a soft fabric

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of feel, as in thought or believed
second meaning: a matted woollen cloth

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past of feel, meaning believed, and the name of a pressed woollen cloth.

clue.text: Dwelling on tense vote in favour

indicators.note: in a down clue the dwelling sits on top of the tense letter

parts.note: a place is a home or dwelling
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Living somewhere while a tense vote is taken in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A placet is a Latin-derived term for an assenting vote in a university or church assembly.

clue.text: Sad that Spain has invaded a foreign port

indicators.note: the country letter has invaded, gone inside, the word for sad

parts.note: triste is French, and an old English word, for sad
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A gloomy note that Spain once invaded a port abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Triste is French for sad, also found in English as a literary word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a seaport on the Adriatic in north-east Italy, so it is a port abroad.

clue.text: They don't make the film, dates having been switched

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase change places, so the second word comes first

parts.note: someone who dates another takes them out

explanation.surface: Discarded footage, with the release dates swapped around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dates' looks like calendar days, but it is the verb: to date someone is to take them out, and swapping that phrase's two words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Outtakes are scenes filmed but cut from the finished picture, so they never make it into the movie.

clue.text: What we are called in explosive competition

indicators.note: our name goes inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
what we are called is our name

explanation.surface: A team's name being dropped into a fiery, explosive contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a series of contests between players or teams, a competition for a prize.

clue.text: Time goose should be cooked in foil

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: when it is time, the goose should be cooked wrapped in foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like kitchen foil to wrap the goose; it is the comic's foil, the partner who sets up jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a comedian's straight man, the foil whose role is to make the lead look funny.

clue.text: Rock purveyor we will make rude noises about

indicators.note: the jeering word goes about, around, the contraction

parts.note: to jeer is to mock with rude shouts
we will contracts to we'll

explanation.surface: A rock concert seller is warned of being booed and catcalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music; here it is slang for a gem, so the purveyor sells jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks is slang for diamonds or gems, and a jeweller is someone who sells them.

clue.text: Sprinter in bar bent back to grasp nuts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Usain Bolt, the Jamaican sprinter, written with his initial

definitions.text: bar bent back to grasp nuts
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a U-shaped threaded rod fastened with nuts

explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub serving nuts; it is a metal rod bent into a U.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixture is a rod bent into the shape of a letter U, and the sprinter is Usain Bolt by initial.

clue.text: Scots knew England's garden?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Scots, ken means know and this is its past tense
second meaning: the county called the Garden of England

explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the south-eastern English county nicknamed the Garden of England for its orchards and hop fields.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a Scots past tense of ken, to know, and a fruit-growing county famed as England's garden.

clue.text: Author as boxer, could one say — heavyweight

parts.note: a chest is a box, so one who boxes things might jokingly be called a chester
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A writer described as a heavyweight boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton was an English author famed for the Father Brown stories, and was himself a very large man.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English writer of essays, poems and detective stories, so he is an author.

clue.text: Childish type, endlessly dim, breaking equipment

indicators.note: the trimmed word breaks into the kit, splitting it

parts.note: kit is gear, equipment

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the word for dim

parts.note: dull means dim

explanation.surface: A rather dim child-like person, breaking all the equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts DULL to DUL, which goes into KIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidult is an adult with youthful tastes, such as games or toys, a grown-up who acts childishly.

clue.text: Hunt neared ground, positioned for concealment?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunt has closed in on its quarry, which has gone to ground in hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the earth the fox hides in, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed beneath another is hidden by it, so being below is a position for concealment.

clue.text: Invite to relax and steal from church?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a casual invitation to sit down
second meaning: read literally, to take away a church bench

explanation.walkthrough: A pew is a church bench, so taking one literally would be stealing from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for sitting down, and a pew is the long wooden seat of a church.

clue.text: Indistinct notice with garish border

indicators.note: the garish word forms a border around the notice

parts.note: showy means flashy, garish
an ad is an advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: A vague advert with a gaudy frame around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy means vague and hard to make out, as if seen in shade.

clue.text: Distortion isn't commonly cosmetic

parts.note: a warp is a twist or distortion
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Twisting isn't a common type of cosmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a noun naming face paint, so 'cosmetic' is used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is used jokingly for make-up, a cosmetic applied before going out.

clue.text: Slander, heartlessly audacious in itself

indicators.note: heartlessly removes all the inner letters of audacious, leaving its ends

parts.note: first and last letters of audacious
per se is Latin for in itself

explanation.surface: A slander that is cruel and audacious in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to attack their reputation with false charges, the act of slandering.

clue.text: Aching to suppress German city university

indicators.note: the aching word holds down, suppresses, the city by enclosing it

parts.note: sore means aching
Bonn is a city in Germany, once the West German capital

explanation.surface: Aches being suppressed by a German city's university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the historic seat of the University of Paris, so it is a university.

clue.text: Stagger about, 'run out' replaced by 'stumped'

indicators.note: out and replaced by mean the run letter is taken out and the stumped letters take its place

parts.note: around means about
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer changes a 'run out' into 'stumped' and staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring, R is a run and ST marks a batsman out stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze or shock them, a close synonym of astound.

clue.text: Cathedral search resolved: it's right in the centre

indicators.note: the right letters go into the middle of the rearranged word
resolved means sorted out, so the letters of search are rearranged

explanation.surface: A search of a cathedral is solved once the right thing turns up at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is only a link here: the right letters sit at the centre of the rearranged search.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a French city whose Gothic cathedral is famed for its stained glass.

clue.text: The peak hour, dinner time?

parts.note: eight o'clock is a typical time for dinner

explanation.surface: Dinner at the busiest hour is the high point of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The peak' reads as a noun, as in the height of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Height means the high point or summit, as in the height of the season.

clue.text: God posed with big pot of tea

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed
an urn is a large vessel for tea

explanation.surface: A deity sat for a portrait with a huge teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the Roman god of agriculture and time, father of Jupiter.

clue.text: Uncompromising boss ultimately deceived on Radio 4

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of boss

parts.note: last letter of boss

indicators.note: on the radio a word is heard, not seen, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: tricked means deceived

explanation.surface: A tough boss is fooled live on BBC Radio 4.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, S plus TRICKED sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict means rigidly enforcing rules, unwilling to bend, so uncompromising.

clue.text: Screen addict perhaps, one contorted with grimace

indicators.note: contorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A screen addict, face twisted into a grimace.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinemagoer watches films at the cinema, and one hooked on the big screen is an example.

clue.text: Youngster spends year on benefit

indicators.note: spends means gives away, so the year letter leaves the youngster

parts.note: a boy is a youngster

explanation.surface: A young person spends a year on benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or advantage, something that is of benefit.

clue.text: Start to bash away in contest

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of bash

parts.note: first letter of bash
out means away, not at home

explanation.surface: Kicking off a contest with a bash away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a single fight or match, especially in boxing, so a contest.

clue.text: Suddenly discover hotel is losing pounds

indicators.note: losing means the pounds letter is dropped

parts.note: Hilton is a hotel chain
L is the abbreviation for pounds (libra)

explanation.surface: A hotel's finances show it losing money.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to find it by chance, to come upon it suddenly.

clue.text: Short walk in once moving moonlit scene

indicators.note: the walk goes inside the rearranged letters
moving means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a turn is a short stroll

explanation.surface: A short walk once made through a moving moonlit landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is an old-fashioned word for a short stroll, as in taking a turn round the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a painting of a night scene, as in Whistler's Thames pictures.
